Why go: watching elephants be elephants

Koh Samui has moved away from elephant riding, but many so-called sanctuaries still sell bathing and close handling. This visit goes further: you watch from a raised skywalk and viewing areas while the elephants feed, wander and roll in the mud, and a guide explains each animal's background and the welfare standards behind the programme. It is the most hands-off elephant experience we offer.

What you'll do

After a short conservation briefing you walk the 400 m skywalk above the elephants' area, then move to the viewing point for the mud bath, where the elephants cool off and protect their skin. There is plenty of time for questions and photos. There is no riding and you do not get into the water with the animals; if a feeding moment is offered, the keepers lead it and ask guests to look out for the smaller elephants.

Who it suits

  • Travellers who care about animal welfare and want an elephant visit they can feel good about.
  • Families with children from 5 and photographers (bring a zoom lens).

Who should choose something else

  • If preparing food and hand-feeding is important to your children, the 4x4 safari with elephant feeding includes it, plus a waterfall and viewpoints.
  • Anyone with limited mobility: the skywalk has steps and slopes.

Good to know

  • Behaviour: keep your distance from mothers with calves, stay quiet near the animals, and no alcohol or drugs on site.
  • Clothing: neutral colours, closed shoes and insect repellent, especially after rain.
  • Weather: the programme runs in light rain; October to December afternoons can be very wet, so the morning slot is safer then.

How it compares

Compared with the feeding-focused programmes on the island, this visit is shorter on contact and longer on explanation, with the skywalk giving a view of how the elephants move as a group. If your children are under 5, ask us first, as there is no published price for them.
